source_review: Scratch store serializes dedup/accounting; files are immutable and value copies own their snapshots. Snapshot coding contexts and decode budget remain synchronous and confined to each call.
A failed close or partial write cannot publish a blob. Failed unlink stays conservatively charged to the limit; normal last-owner release deletes blobs/directory.
Disk budget includes old/new snapshot ownership during a transaction; a full budget can reject a new edit rather than discard old history.
Scratch I/O and history restoration are synchronous. Active document, index overhead and other live session copies are not covered by the per-session resident payload limit.
